name: visual-impression
description: Restore the AI coding conversation that was running in each terminal, per project. Works locally and over Remote SSH.

untrustedWorkspaces.description: The extension records terminals and resumes agent conversations. It never runs anything from the workspace, but a workspace setting could point its index at a path of the workspace's choosing, so that one setting is ignored until the workspace is trusted.

virtualWorkspaces.description: It reads the agent's transcripts and the process table on the machine the terminals are on, so it needs a real filesystem.

commands.title: Visual Impression: Remember the terminal layout
Visual Impression: Forget this workspace's history

visualImpression.promptOnStartup.description: When a project is opened and agent terminals were recorded here before, offer to bring them back.

visualImpression.scanIntervalSeconds.description: How often to re-check which agent each terminal is running. An agent started inside an existing terminal is picked up on the next scan.

visualImpression.historyDays.description: Forget terminals that closed more than this many days ago.

visualImpression.showPreviews.markdownDescription: Show a line of each conversation -- its title and its last prompt -- in the picker and in the status report, read from the agent's own transcript on this machine. Turn it off to list conversations by terminal name alone, for instance when the screen is being shared.

visualImpression.stateDirectory.markdownDescription: Where to keep the per-project index. Empty means `~/.visual-impression`. A `~` at the start is your home directory. An index left behind by an earlier version in `~/.wt-tabs/vscode` is moved here once, automatically.

enumDescriptions: Only when 'Visual Impression: Remember the terminal layout' is run. Focus never moves on its own.
Also read it by itself after the window has been out of focus for a while. Focus ends up in the terminal that was active.
Never read it; restores are grouped by the setting below instead.
visualImpression.rememberLayout.markdownDescription: Whether to read which terminals share a tab, so a restore can rebuild the arrangement. VS Code does not report this; the only way to read it is to step focus through the panes, and the API cannot say where focus was beforehand, so after a reading focus is in a terminal. `manual` reads only when the command is run. `onBlur` also reads by itself once the window has been out of focus for `#visualImpression.rememberLayoutAfterSeconds#`, stops the moment the window is used again, and hands focus to the terminal that was active -- choose it only if that is where you type.

visualImpression.rememberLayoutAfterSeco.markdownDescription: In `onBlur` mode, how long the window must have been out of focus before the arrangement is read. A glance at another window should not start a walk that your return then interrupts.

visualImpression.restoreTerminalsPerTab.markdownDescription: When a restore has to open new terminals, how many to place side by side as splits in one tab. VS Code does not let an extension read the layout a project had, so this is the shape it falls back to. Set it to `1` for one tab per terminal, or give a list such as `[2, 1, 3]` to say how many panes each tab gets -- the last entry repeats.

visualImpression.reuseRevivedTerminals.description: When restoring, resume into a terminal VS Code revived by itself rather than opening another one. This is what keeps a split layout: VS Code rebuilds the arrangement, and a conversation resumed into one of those terminals lands inside it.
